name: Task_2
description:
Study the glass transition of sodium silicate during cooling and reheating, and assess how the thermal history affects the inferred transition temperature. Start from the supplied equilibrated state at 1300 K. Use the supplied BKS-type Buckingham-Coulomb potential with PPPM electrostatics in LAMMPS, real units, charge atom style, periodic boundaries, and isotropic NPT dynamics at zero target pressure throughout.

Cool continuously from 1300 K to 300 K at 50 K/ps for 20 ps, hold at 300 K for 10 ps, then reheat continuously to 1300 K at 50 K/ps for 20 ps. At a 1 fs timestep this is 20,000 cooling, 10,000 hold, and 20,000 reheating steps. Carry the same system through all stages without replacing atoms or reinitializing velocities. Choose and document suitable integration, thermostat, barostat, and sampling settings. Record elapsed time, target and measured temperature, pressure, and density at sufficient resolution to examine each stage and reproduce the analysis.

Estimate the cooling and reheating glass-transition temperatures from the density response using measured temperature as the temperature coordinate. Choose and document your estimator and the data it uses. Report both transition estimates and their signed difference, reheating minus cooling, in kelvin. For the 300 K hold, report representative mean temperature and density and quantify density drift using justified analysis windows. Assess the evidence for equilibration and explain any limitations of interpreting the observed transition or hold behavior, including the short hold and rapid ramps.

Keep a restartable state at each stage boundary. Each state must preserve the cell, atom IDs, positions, charges, velocities, and elapsed time. Record the exact data ranges and method used for each transition estimate.
submission_format: Submit the path to your completed manifest.json file. Use the blank example as a guide. Paths inside the manifest may be relative to the manifest file.
